title: Thai Stew with Earthy Flavors
description: A hearty Thai stew made with a variety of earthy ingredients, perfect for a cold evening. The stew's velvety texture and rich flavors will transport you to the streets of Bangkok.

ingredients.name: Polish Sausage
ingredients.notes: Slice the sausage into thin rounds before adding to the stew

ingredients.name: Earthy Mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Use a variety of mushrooms such as shiitake and cremini

ingredients.name: Stew Vegetables
ingredients.notes: Add your favorite vegetables such as carrots, potatoes, and bell peppers

ingredients.name: Velvety Coconut Milk
ingredients.notes: Full-fat coconut milk adds richness and creaminess to the stew

ingredients.name: Thai Curry Paste
ingredients.notes: Use a high-quality curry paste for the best flavor

ingredients.name: Fish Sauce
ingredients.notes: Add a splash of fish sauce for depth of flavor

ingredients.name: Brown Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the heat from the curry paste with a touch of sweetness

ingredients.name: Rice Vinegar
ingredients.notes: Add a splash of rice vinegar for brightness and acidity

ingredients.name: Coconut Oil
ingredients.notes: Use coconut oil for its high smoke point and rich flavor

ingredients.name: Fresh Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving

instructions: Heat the coconut oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the sliced Polish sausage and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove the sausage from the pot and set aside.
Add the Thai curry paste to the pot and cook for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the stew vegetables, mushrooms, and fish sauce to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes, until the vegetables start to soften.
Add the coconut milk, brown sugar, and rice vinegar to the pot. Stir to combine.
Return the cooked sausage to the pot and stir to combine.
Bring the stew to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Serve the stew hot, garnished with fresh cilantro and steamed rice on the side.
Optional: Serve with a side of steamed bok choy or Thai basil for added freshness.
